submission.title: I spent 47 minutes a month on receipts. A local Gemma now does it in 4.

chat.content: What does this jury care about most?

Writing, mortal. The brief says it plainly: writing quality is weighted most heavily. Then relevance to the theme, then creativity, and only then technical execution.

So: a clear story of one annoyance, a measured result, a demo, and an honest “why open innovation matters” section. A brilliant build with a dull post loses to a modest build told well.

Receipt Sloth. It scored 78 to the standup bot's 64, it fits Best Use of Gemma, and it has a number hiding in it: minutes per month, before and after. Time yourself this week. That number is your title.

Writing Quality, at 6 of 10, and it carries half the weight. Three moves:
1. First line: the 47 minutes. Not the stack.
2. One GIF under the title: a crumpled receipt becoming a row.
3. Turn your one-line “why open” into four sentences: offline, private, free forever, and the moment that mattered.

winners_did: Made a measured claim the hook of the title itself: “82% vs 79%” is impossible to scroll past
Opened with one specific moment of pain (a snoozed alarm, a confusing form) before any architecture
Showed the real thing working in a video, not only screenshots
Explained exactly where the open model beat a closed one, with a concrete example
you_did_well: Your final title carried a measured result: 47 minutes down to 4
Your “why open innovation matters” section was specific: receipts never leave your laptop
A live demo, a repo and a CI workflow: the jury could check everything
lessons: Put the measured result in the title from the very first draft
Open with one specific moment of pain, before any architecture
Record a 30-second video of the real thing working
debrief.count_says: You lost to sharper storytellers, not better builders. Learn the craft, mortal, and the next jury is yours.
